paras: On Sunday, Ravi and his sister Meera went to the pond. Ravi made a paper boat and put it on the water. It floated. Then Meera dropped a small stone into the pond. Splash! The stone sank to the bottom.

“Why did my boat float but your stone sink?” asked Ravi. Their father smiled. “The boat is light and wide, so the water can hold it up. The stone is heavy for its small size, so the water cannot hold it up.”

The next morning, Ravi saw his shadow on the ground. It was very long. “Look, I am a giant!” he laughed. At noon, he stood in the same place. Now his shadow was short and small. “Where did my shadow go?” he asked.
Meera said, “A shadow is made when something blocks the sunlight. In the morning the sun is low in the sky, so shadows are long. At noon the sun is high above us, so shadows are short.”
In the evening it rained. Ravi ran into the lane and slipped on the mud. “Oops!” he said. Meera helped him up. “Why did I slip?” asked Ravi. “The road was dry in the morning, and you did not slip.”
Their father explained, “Water and mud make the ground slippery, so our feet cannot hold on to it. This is why we must walk slowly on wet ground.”

items.q: Why did the paper boat float but the stone sink?
items.a: The boat is light and wide, so the water holds it up. The stone is heavy for its size, so it sinks.

items.q: When is our shadow long, and when is it short?
items.a: It is long in the morning, when the sun is low. It is short at noon, when the sun is high above us.

items.q: Why did Ravi slip in the lane?
items.a: Water and mud make the ground slippery, so his feet could not hold on.

items.q: Name two things that float and two things that sink in water.
items.a: Any correct examples. Float: leaf, paper boat, wooden stick, ball. Sink: stone, coin, key.
